b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Trade and Ports
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the 19th century, and he asks how trade changed the cities.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened as trade grew.
cues: Say that trade grew, with a medida que
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.target: A medida que crecía el comercio, crecían los puertos y las ciudades.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.english: As trade grew, the ports and the cities grew.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-01.canDo: I can use *a medida que* and *cuanto más… más* to say how one change grew with another.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Lerdo Law
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading about the Reforma in Mexico and asks what the Lerdo Law required.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what had to be sold.
cues: Say what had to be sold
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.target: Las tierras de la Iglesia y de las comunidades tenían que ser vendidas.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.english: The lands of the Church and of the communities had to be sold.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-02.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* (*fue aprobada*, *fueron vendidas*) to say what the liberal reforms did.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Church and State in Ecuador
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about the Church, and Carlos asks about Ecuador in 1869.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what was necessary to be a citizen.
cues: Say what was necessary, with se
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.target: En Ecuador se necesitaba ser católico para ser ciudadano.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.english: In Ecuador it was necessary to be Catholic to be a citizen.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-03.canDo: I can use impersonal *se* (*se decidió*, *se necesitaba*, *se podía*) to say what was decided and what was possible.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Immigrants at the Ports
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum about immigration, and she asks how the immigrants arrived.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.prompt: Tell Meg how the immigrants arrived.
cues: Say that they arrived at the ports
Say what they were looking for, with a gerund
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.target: Los inmigrantes llegaban a los puertos buscando trabajo.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.english: The immigrants arrived at the ports looking for work.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-04.canDo: I can use the gerund to say what two actions were happening at the same time.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides of Modernization
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you to sum up the liberal period for a class.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos the two sides of the period.
cues: Say one gain, with por un lado
Say one limit, with por otro lado
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.target: Por un lado, crecieron las ciudades; por otro lado, muchas personas quedaron sin tierra.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.english: On the one hand, the cities grew; on the other hand, many people were left without land.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-05.canDo: I can use ordering markers (*primero*, *además*, *por un lado… por otro lado*, *por último*) to organise an explanation of the liberal period.

b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Liberals
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class, and she asks what the liberals wanted.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.prompt: Tell Meg what the liberals wanted.
cues: Say what they wanted for the citizens
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.target: Los liberales querían leyes iguales para todos los ciudadanos.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.english: The liberals wanted equal laws for all citizens.
b1-liberalismomodernizacion-consolidatio.canDo: I can talk about liberalism with *a medida que* and *cuanto más… más*, the passive with *ser*, impersonal *se*, the gerund and ordering markers.
